title: map, filter, reduce
objective: Transform, filter and sort arrays with map, filter, reduce, find, some, every and sort
story: You're deep in the Function Nebula, captain. The radar lists hundreds of stars; instead of walking through them one by one with a loop, we'll give arrays superpowers like **map, filter and reduce**.

sections.title: map: transform every item
filter, find, some and every
sections.body:
`filter` makes a new array from the items that pass a condition. If the function returns `true` the item stays; if `false` it's dropped:

```js
const fuel = [80, 15, 60, 5];
const low = fuel.filter((f) => f < 20);   // [15, 5]
const first = fuel.find((f) => f < 20);   // 15
const none = fuel.find((f) => f > 100);   // undefined
fuel.some((f) => f < 10);                 // true
fuel.every((f) => f > 0);                 // true
```

- `find` gives **the first matching item**, not an array; `undefined` if none matches.
- `some`: `true` if **at least one** matches.
- `every`: `true` if **all** match.

sections.title: reduce: boil it down to one value
sections.body:
`reduce` walks through the whole array and produces **a single value**: a total, the largest value, a counter... You give it two things: a function and a starting value.

```js
const stars = [3, 5, 2];
const total = stars.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s, 0);
console.log(total); // 10
```

The function's first parameter (here `sum`) is the value **built up so far**, the second is the next item. Step by step: 0 + 3 = 3, 3 + 5 = 8, 8 + 2 = 10.

Don't forget the starting value (`0`); with arrays of objects it's a must:

```js
const tanks = [{ fuel: 40 }, { fuel: 25 }];
const all = tanks.reduce((sum, t) => sum + t.fuel, 0); // 65
```

sections.title: sort and chaining
sections.body:
`sort` sorts an array, but careful: it compares items **like text**! For numbers, give it a compare function:

```js
[10, 9, 100].sort();                  // [10, 100, 9]  wrong!
[10, 9, 100].sort((a, b) => a - b);   // [9, 10, 100]  smallest first
[10, 9, 100].sort((a, b) => b - a);   // [100, 10, 9]  biggest first
```

If the function returns a negative number `a` goes first; if positive, `b` goes first. To sort objects by a field: `players.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)`.

`sort` **changes the original array**. If you want to keep the original, copy it first with `slice()`: `scores.slice().sort(...)`.

Because these methods return arrays, they can be **chained** one after another:

```js
const winners = players
  .filter((p) => p.score > 50)
  .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
  .map((p) => p.name);
```

tasks.title: Double speed
tasks.prompt: Create a new array called `doubled` by **multiplying every speed** in `speeds` **by 2**. Use `map`; `speeds` must not change.

tasks.title: Sorting signals
tasks.prompt:
Sort out the radar signals:

1. `strong`: a new array of the signals that are 30 or more (`filter`).
2. `firstWeak`: the **first** signal below 10 (`find`).
hints: find gives the first matching item: signals.find((s) => s < 10)

tasks.title: Total fuel
tasks.prompt:
Add up the fuel in all the tanks with `reduce` and store it in `total`. Then calculate the average in `average` (total / number of tanks).

Output: `Total fuel: 105` and `Average: 35`

challenge.title: Score analysis
challenge.prompt:
Analyze the `scores` array, but `scores` **must not change**:

- `sorted`: a copy sorted from smallest to biggest (`[7, 9, 25, 40, 100]`). Use a compare function!
- `top3`: the 3 highest scores, biggest first (`[100, 40, 25]`). Hint: `slice(0, 3)` gives the first 3 items.
- `allPassed`: are all scores greater than 5? (`every`)
- `hasPerfect`: is there a score of 100? (`some`)
hints: Copy first with slice(): scores.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b)

project_task.title: Leaderboard
project_task.prompt:
Build the game's leaderboard. Write the `leaderboard(list)` function:

- It sorts the players by score from **highest to lowest**,
- returns an **array** of texts like `"1. Emma - 150"` (the position comes from `map`'s second parameter),
- and the order of the original `list` array must not change (copy it first with `slice()`).
hints: Don't forget return in the function.
